test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In which part of the Constitution are fundamental duties added?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV-A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A of the Constitution of India**, which forms a part of **Part IV A,** outlines the fundamental duties of Indian citizens.
 
• Enacted through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**, this section enumerates eleven fundamental duties:
 
 
• Adhere to the Indian Constitution and honor its principles and institutions, as well as the National Flag and the National Anthem. Embrace and follow the noble ideals that fueled the national struggle for independence.
 
• Uphold and safeguard the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Defend the nation and provide national service when required.
 
• Foster harmony and a sense of brotherhood among all Indian citizens, transcending religious, linguistic, regional, or sectional differences, and renounce practices demeaning to women.
 
• Appreciate and conserve the diverse heritage of the country's composite culture.
 
• Preserve and enhance the natural environment, encompassing forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife, and demonstrate compassion towards living beings.
 
• Cultivate a scientific mindset, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• Protect public property and refrain from resorting to violence. Strive for excellence in both individual and collective endeavors, thereby advancing the nation to greater levels of achievement.
 
 
 
• Additionally, the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 introduced an eleventh duty: Provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Part III** safeguards the Fundamental Rights granted to Indian citizens and, in certain instances, to all individuals.
 
• **Part II** outlines the citizenship provisions, determining the individuals who hold citizenship at the Constitution's inception and establishing specific conditions for those affected by the partition of the country.
 
• **Part I**, known as "The Union and Its Territories," comprises laws pertaining to the constitution of India as a nation and the union of states forming it.
